display_title: Add jax.lax.exp2m1 and log2p1.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.lax.exp2m1 and log2p1.

Computing `2**x - 1` as `jax.lax.exp2(x) - 1` or `log2(1 + x)` as `jax.lax.log2(1 + x)` loses precision for `x` near zero because adding or subtracting `1` cancels significant bits. Rewriting them as `expm1(x * log(2))` or `log1p(x) / log(2)` avoids cancellation near zero, but multiplying or dividing by `log(2)` adds an extra rounding step and can miss exact values when `x` or `1 + x` is an integer power of two.

Add `jax.lax.exp2m1` and `jax.lax.log2p1` (and their core primitives) to compute `2**x - 1` and `log2(1 + x)` directly on real floating-point arrays, as specified by IEEE 754-2019.

display_title: Add a more accurate default implementation for `lax.erfc` behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
Add a more accurate default implementation for `lax.erfc` behind a flag.

Currently, default-accuracy `lax.erfc` uses `chlo.erfc` on `float16`, `float32`, and `float64`. `chlo.erfc` switches between multiple range-specific polynomials and divisions, reaches up to 66.5 ULPs of error in `float32` (157 ULPs on TPU) and at least 350 ULPs in `float64` due to rounding `x^2` before `exp(-x^2)`, and drops subnormal outputs to zero.

Add a temporary `jax_accurate_default_erfc` config flag (`default=False`; `HIGHEST` accuracy mode is unchanged):
- `float16` and `bfloat16`: compute the result in `float32` using a degree-4 or degree-6 polynomial in `1 / (|x| + 2)`.
- `float32`: split `x^2` into an exact high part and a small remainder (`s_hi + s_lo`), compute the exponential using `exp2` on GPU and TPU (or `exp` on CPU) times a short polynomial correction for the remainder, and multiply by a degree-8 polynomial in `1 / (|x| + 2)`.
- `float64`: split `x^2` into `s_hi + s_lo`, multiply `exp(-s_hi)` by a degree-2 correction polynomial for `s_lo`, and multiply by a degree-20 polynomial in `1 / (|x| + 4) - 9/64`.

With the flag enabled, `lax.erfc` uses fewer ops than `chlo.erfc`, preserves subnormal outputs on CPU and GPU, returns `1.0` at `+-0.0`, and reduces error to at most 7.0 ULPs on CPU, 7.5 ULPs on GPU, 69.0 ULPs on TPU v2–v5e, 62.5 ULPs on TPU v5p, 9.5 ULPs on TPU v6e, and 9.0 ULPs on TPU 7x across all `float32` inputs, and 10.0 ULPs on sampled `float64` inputs on CPU and GPU.

jax.scipy.fft.dct: use rfft for real input

The input to the FFT is real, so its spectrum is conjugate-symmetric; rfft

Non-float inputs are promoted with promote_dtypes_inexact before the rfft,
so output dtypes match the previous C2C path (64-bit integers still give
float64 under x64); float16/bfloat16 are widened to float32.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Cache the per-primitive `jit` objects in eager `shard_map`

head_commit.message:
Cache the per-primitive `jit` objects in eager `shard_map`

Eager `shard_map` (outside of `jit`, or under `jax.disable_jit()`) runs
each primitive, and each input/output reshard, as
`api.jit(HashablePartial(...))`. The `jit` object was created fresh on
every call, so its tracing and lowering caches started empty and every
primitive was lowered and compiled again on every call, even though the
`HashablePartial` arguments were the same.

Cache the `jit` objects with `util.cache`, keyed on the
`HashablePartial` (and `out_shardings`), like
`dispatch.xla_primitive_callable` does for op-by-op dispatch. A second
call of the same eager `shard_map` now does no lowering.

display_title: [Mosaic GPU][NFC] Flatten tcgen05.mma K-stepping onto SmemDescriptor.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU][NFC] Flatten tcgen05.mma K-stepping onto SmemDescriptor.

`tcgen05.mma` previously partitioned K into uniform `k_group_elems` chunks in an outer loop while `_do_mma` stepped instructions within each K group using a fixed `scale_steps` divisor. With `SmemDescriptor` handling arbitrary K element offsets across SMEM tile boundaries, the outer K-group and single-tile M-group loops are redundant and block upcoming mixed-width MMA K steps on SM103.

Collapse `tcgen05.mma` to loop only over `n_groups`, pass the full `m` and `k` extents into `_do_mma`, and compute TMEM operand, sparse metadata, and block-scale column and selector offsets directly from each instruction's cumulative K element offset rather than `scale_steps`.

head_commit.message:
Pin down reduction numerics (e.g. jnp.sum, jnp.dot) by specifying reduction_order etc

Before this CL, operations like `jnp.sum` didn't have bitwise/0-ULP semantics because the reduction order is not specified in the operation and is instead chosen by XLA. Pallas kernels specify across-tile reductions, but within-tile reductions are still chosen by Mosaic. The goal here is to provide a way for the programmer to specify the exact numerical behavior, allowing hardware-efficient reduction orders of practical interest.

In general, each reduction order along an axis of size N can be identified with a rooted binary tree with N leaves. But not all of those are practically interesting. We restrict ourselves to (non-binary) 'level-homogeneous' trees, where at each level the sibling subtrees have the same arity and identical topology. Such trees can be evaluated efficiently by uniform hardware loops and SIMD-style instructions.

In more concrete NumPy terms, these reduction orders look like splitting the axis to be reduced in two, choosing which sub-axis to sum first, and (recursively) choosing a reduction order for each sub-axis. The base cases are primitive orders, like linear left-to-right order or within-tile hardware intrinsics.

But there's a bit more to the space than just reduction order, since reductions might involve intermediate dtype casts, like casting to bf16 before doing cross-device reduction. We also need a case to handle bidirectional ring reductions. So our language logically ends up looking like

```haskell
data PadVal = Zero | Absent

data PrimitiveOrder
  = Auto
  | Linear            -- (((x0 + x1) + x2) + ...)
  | Intrinsic String  -- "tpu_v7_mxu_256", "tpu_xlane_128"

data Split = Block Int | Strided Int

data RingDir  = Asc | Desc | BiDir
data PermSpec = Ring Int RingDir  -- Ring outAxis dir

data RedExpr
  = Fold    PrimitiveOrder Dtype
  | Cast    Dtype     RedExpr
  | Pad     Int       PadVal   RedExpr
  | Tile    Split     RedExpr  RedExpr
  | Permute PermSpec  RedExpr
```

where the `Auto` primitive allows for the backend to choose an order (hence allowing partial constraints on reduction order; spelled `"unordered"` / `Unordered` in the implementation below), and `Absent` pads unused lanes with `-0.0` rather than `+0.0` because `-0.0` is the true IEEE-754 RNE additive identity (`(-0.0) + (-0.0) = -0.0` and `x + (-0.0) = x` for every finite `x`, whereas `(-0.0) + (+0.0) = +0.0` flips the sign of `-0.0`). The semantics are roughly

```python
def eval_red(e: RedExpr, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
  # sum along leading axis of `X` according to RedExpr `e`
  match e:
    case Fold(Linear(), dt):
      return functools.reduce(np.add, X.astype(dt))
    case Fold(Intrinsic(name), dt):
      return eval_intrinsic(name, dt, X)
    case Cast(dt, body):
      return eval_red(body, X).astype(dt)
    case Pad(m, fill, body):
      v = -0.0 if fill == 'absent' else +0.0  # -0.0 is IEEE-754 RNE + id!
      pad = np.full(((-len(X)) % m, *X.shape[1:]), v, X.dtype)
      return eval_red(body, np.concatenate([X, pad]))
    case Tile(Block(b), inner, outer):
      cs = [X[i : i + b] for i in range(0, len(X), b)]
      return eval_red(outer, np.stack([eval_red(inner, c) for c in cs]))
```

In more concrete NumPy terms, these reduction orders look like splitting the axis to be reduced in two, choosing which sub-axis to sum first, and (recursively) choosing a reduction order for each sub-axis.   = Auto
```haskell
  | Linear            -- (((x0 + x1) + x2) + ...)
  | Intrinsic String  -- "tpu_v7_mxu_256", "tpu_xlane_128"

data Split = Block Int | Strided Int

  | Permute PermSpec  RedExpr
```

[remat] Support passing static arguments as keyword arguments in jax.checkpoint

When a function decorated with jax.checkpoint (or jax.remat) was called with arguments passed as keyword arguments (e.g. f(x, flag=False) where flag is in static_argnums or static_argnames), jax.checkpoint failed with a ValueError or TracerBoolConversionError because static_argnums indices did not match len(args).

This change binds incoming args and kwargs to the function signature when kwargs are passed or when default arguments are omitted, resolving them to positional slots and populating defaults. It also ensures static_argnames is converted to static argument indices and is supported in both checkpoint and remat.

Fixes #18405.

In general, each reduction order along an axis of size N can be identified with a rooted binary tree with N leaves. But not all of those are practically interesting. We restrict ourselves to (non-binary) 'level-homogeneous' trees, where at each level the sibling subtrees have the same arity and identical topology. Such trees can be evaluated efficiently by uniform hardware loops and SIMD-style instructions.

In more concrete NumPy terms, these reduction orders look like splitting the axis to be reduced in two, choosing which sub-axis to sum first, and (recursively) choosing a reduction order for each sub-axis. The base cases are primitive orders, like linear left-to-right order or within-tile hardware intrinsics.

But there's a bit more to the space than just reduction order, since reductions might involve intermediate dtype casts, like casting to bf16 before doing cross-device reduction. We also need a case to handle bidirectional ring reductions. So our language logically ends up looking like

```haskell
data PadVal = Zero | Absent

data PrimitiveOrder
  = Auto
  | Linear            -- (((x0 + x1) + x2) + ...)
  | Intrinsic String  -- "tpu_v7_mxu_256", "tpu_xlane_128"

data Split = Block Int | Strided Int

data RingDir  = Asc | Desc | BiDir

  | Cast    Dtype     RedExpr
  | Pad     Int       PadVal   RedExpr
  | Tile    Split     RedExpr  RedExpr
  | Permute PermSpec  RedExpr
```

```python
    case Cast(dt, body):

    case Pad(m, fill, body):

      pad = np.full(((-len(X)) % m, *X.shape[1:]), v, X.dtype)
      return eval_red(body, np.concatenate([X, pad]))
    case Tile(Block(b), inner, outer):
      cs = [X[i : i + b] for i in range(0, len(X), b)]

    case Permute(Ring(out_axis, dir), body):
      return eval_red(body, ring_perm(X, out_axis, dir))
```

display_title: Speed up jax.random.gamma on CPU by running the rejection loop in batches

head_commit.message:
Run the gamma sampler's rejection loop in batches on CPU

Since the CPU lowering of random_gamma_p switched to a single vmap
(#22678), every element runs the Marsaglia-Tsang rejection loops until
the slowest element of the whole array is accepted, so the time grows
faster than the number of elements. On CPU, run the rejection loop with
lax.map(..., batch_size=16) instead, keeping the per-element setup and
the final transform vmapped over the whole array. This makes gamma, beta
and dirichlet sampling about 2x faster for 1e4 elements and 4-7x faster
for 1e6 to 1e7 elements.

Each element keeps its own key, so the samples are unchanged. The
lowering on other platforms is unchanged.

Fixes #18984.

display_title: Fix eigh_tridiagonal when the first off-diagonal element is zero

head_commit.message:
Fix eigh_tridiagonal when the first off-diagonal element is zero

The first step of the Sturm count perturbed q only by (eps * |e[0]|)**2
when the bisection point x equals d[0]. If e[0] is zero, or that square
underflows, q stays 0 and the next step computes 0/0, so the eigenvalue
count is wrong and bisection converges to wrong eigenvalues (and inverse
iteration to wrong eigenvectors). Integer diagonals hit x == d[0] exactly.

Use the same pivmin rule for the first step as for the others, as LAPACK's
dlaebz does.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.scipy.special.kn for integer-order modified Bessel functions of the second kind.

Provide `jax.scipy.special.kn(n, z)` to compute the modified Bessel function of the second kind of integer order `n` for real and complex arguments, complementing `jn`, `yn`, and `iv`.

For positive real arguments, orders 0 and 1 are evaluated in double-word arithmetic across three regimes: the ascending power series and harmonic-number sum (DLMF 10.31.1-10.31.2) for small arguments (`z <= 2`), Temme/Campbell-Miller backward recurrence on the confluent hypergeometric `U(1/2, 1, 2z)` representation (DLMF 10.39.2) normalized by its series sum `sum_{k>=0} p_k` in the intermediate transition region (`2 < z < R_L`), and Hankel's `1/z` asymptotic expansion (DLMF 10.40.2) rescaled by `exp(-z)` for large arguments (`z >= R_L`). Higher orders (`n >= 2`) step upward from `(K_0, K_1)` via the strictly positive forward recurrence `K_{k+1}(z) = (2k / z) K_k(z) + K_{k-1}(z)` in double-word arithmetic with power-of-2 exponent rescaling to avoid intermediate overflow. Complex arguments are evaluated in the first quadrant and extended to all four quadrants via `K_n(conj(z)) = conj(K_n(z))` and `K_n(-z) = (-1)^n K_n(z) - i * pi * I_n(z)`, with forward-mode autodiff supported via `K_0'(z) = -K_1(z)` and `K_n'(z) = -0.5 * (K_{n-1}(z) + K_{n+1}(z))`. Also add integer-order `kn` coverage to the Bessel ULP precision test suite.

display_title: Fix non-termination in `jnp.gcd` and `jnp.lcm` for minimum signed int…

head_commit.message:
Fix non-termination in `jnp.gcd` and `jnp.lcm` for minimum signed integers.

For a signed integer dtype, taking the absolute value of the minimum representable integer (`iinfo(dtype).min`) overflows back to the negative minimum value in two's complement arithmetic. In `jnp.gcd` (and `jnp.lcm`, which delegates to `jnp.gcd`), passing this negative value into the Euclidean `while_loop` produced negative remainders and triggered the post-modulo `x1 < x2` swap whenever the remainder reached zero, swapping zero into `x1` and the negative divisor into `x2` so the loop never terminated (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40840).

Cast `abs(x1)` and `abs(x2)` to the corresponding unsigned integer dtype before computing the greatest common divisor and least common multiple, then convert the result back to the promoted input dtype while preserving weak typing. Also remove the redundant post-modulo comparison swap in the `jnp.gcd` loop body.

Fixes #40840.

display_title: Add `mode="high"` to `jax.random.truncated_normal` to fix tail sampling accuracy.

head_commit.message:
Add `mode="high"` to `jax.random.truncated_normal` to fix tail sampling accuracy.

Previously, `jax.random.truncated_normal` computed inverse-CDF samples by drawing `u ~ uniform(key, shape, dtype, minval=erf(lower / sqrt(2)), maxval=erf(upper / sqrt(2)))` and evaluating `sqrt(2) * erf_inv(u)`. This suffered from several floating-point accuracy issues in the tails:
- `uniform` generated a fixed-point grid of resolution `2^(-nmant)` in `[0, 1)` and rescaled via `floats * (b - a) + a`, cutting off upper-tail probabilities below `2^(-nmant)` on wide intervals, clamping `floats == 0` draws to the lower bound, and losing mantissa bits when adding `a` near ±1 (causing a fraction of draws to round to ±1 and clamp to the far boundary).
- At extreme truncation bounds where `erf` saturates to ±1 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/10951), `a == b == ±1` caused `erf_inv(u)` to return `±inf` and clamp all samples to the wrong boundary.
- For 16-bit dtypes (`bfloat16`, `float16`), native 7-bit/10-bit uniform grids and early `erf` saturation degraded tail accuracy even on moderate bounds.

head_commit.message:
Fix non-termination in `jnp.gcd` and `jnp.lcm` for minimum signed integers.

For a signed integer dtype, taking the absolute value of the minimum representable integer (`iinfo(dtype).min`) overflows back to the negative minimum value in two's complement arithmetic. Cast `abs(x1)` and `abs(x2)` to the corresponding unsigned integer dtype before computing the greatest common divisor and least common multiple, then convert the result back to the promoted input dtype while preserving weak typing. Fixes #40840.

head_commit.message:
Upcast narrow signed integer indices before negative-index wrapping.

Indexing an axis whose length exceeds the maximum value of a narrow signed integer dtype (for example, indexing an axis longer than 127 elements with `jnp.int8(-1)`) previously wrapped the axis length and computed `index + size` within the narrow dtype, overflowing and selecting the wrong element (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42354).

To fix this, we promote narrow signed integer indices to an integer dtype wide enough to represent the target dimension before adding the axis length across dynamic slicing, `NDIndexer` gather/scatter normalization, `jnp.take`, and `jnp.put`. In addition, classify `jax.ds` slices with array or negative start offsets as dynamic slices in eager mode so negative start normalization behaves consistently with `jit`.

Fixes #42354 & #42377

head_commit.message:
[pallas] Zero-initialize paged_attention output for empty sequences when inline_seq_dim=False.

In `paged_flash_attention_kernel` (the `inline_seq_dim=False` path) the
`@pl.when(i == 0)` block that resets `m_ref`, `l_ref` and `o_ref` lives
inside `flash_attention()`, which is itself only executed under
`pl.when(i * bk < length)`. For a sequence with `length == 0` that guard is
already false at `i == 0`, so the output block of that batch slot is never
written and whatever the VMEM output buffer held before (another slot's
activations or uninitialized memory) is copied back to HBM. Nothing traps:
both `pltpu.InterpretParams()` and TPU silently return stale values for the
empty slots, while the non-empty slots are correct.

Zero-length sequences are a supported input: the prefetch logic of the same
kernel explicitly skips them, and the default `inline_seq_dim=True` kernel
zero-initializes unconditionally and returns 0 for them. Hoist the `i == 0`
initialization out of the length guard so both paths agree, and add a test
that empty sequences produce exact zeros for both `inline_seq_dim` values and
all megacore modes.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels.

### Status quo

In the XLA:CPU MLIR fusion pipeline, `f32` `log` uses a handwritten LLVM IR polynomial (`GenerateVF32Log`, 1.19 ULP max error), `f64` `log` falls back to scalar `libm` `log` calls (0.5 ULP, unvectorized), and `log1p` lowers to an algebraic composition around `log` (up to ~3.0 ULP in `f32`).

### Why

Compiling YNNPACK's `log` and `log1p` SIMD kernels (`f32` and `f64`, up to 512-bit vectors) to LLVM bitcode and inlining them during codegen vectorizes `f64` `log` and `log1p`, speeds up `f32` `log` and `log1p` across x86 and ARM64, improves `f32` accuracy (`log` 1.19 -> 1.02 ULP, `log1p` 3.0 -> 1.65 ULP), and deletes XLA:CPU's handwritten `GenerateVF32Log` C++ IR builder.

End-to-end `elementwise_benchmark_test` (`N = 128, 1024, 8192` geomean cycles/op vs baseline):
- `f32` (`BM_LogF32`, `BM_Log1pF32`): `-19.1%` on x86 AVX2+FMA3, `-28.8%` on x86 AVX-512, `-36.6%` on ARM64 NEON.
- `f64` (`BM_LogF64`, `BM_Log1pF64`): `1.7x-4.4x` faster across AVX2, AVX-512, and ARM64 NEON.

### Design choices

- Expose YNNPACK `log` and `log1p` wrappers for `f32` and `f64` vector widths up to 512 bits in `xla/codegen/intrinsic/cpp/ynnpack_unary.{h,cc}`, compile a single `ynnpack_unary_ll` bitcode library, inline from it during codegen, and stop splitting `v16f32` `log` on AVX-512.
- Keep upcasting `f16` and `bf16` to `f32`, since YNNPACK has no native full-precision 16-bit `log`/`log1p` kernels on x86.
- Preserve `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`, and keep the existing `libm` and algebraic `Log1p` lowerings on GPU and when CppGen bitcode is unavailable.

### Compromises

Maximum error bounds in ULPs (from JAX's numerics test suite and `docs/accuracy.md`):

| Op | CPU (before) | CPU (this CL) | NVIDIA GPU | TPU (v6e / 7x) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `log` (`f32`) | 1.5 | 1.5 | 1.0 | 2.5 |
| `log` (`f64`) | 0.5 | 1.5 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log1p` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | 3.0 |
| `log1p` (`f64`) | 2.0 | 2.0 | 1.5 | N/A |
| `log10` (`f32`) | 3.0 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 3.0 |

`pl.when(i * bk < length)`. For a sequence with `length == 0` that guard is
already false at `i == 0`, so the output block of that batch slot is never
written and whatever the VMEM output buffer held before (another slot's

empty slots, while the non-empty slots are correct.

kernel explicitly skips them, and the default `inline_seq_dim=True` kernel
zero-initializes unconditionally and returns 0 for them. Hoist the `i == 0`
initialization out of the length guard so both paths agree, and add a test
that empty sequences produce exact zeros for both `inline_seq_dim` values and
all megacore modes.

head_commit.message:
Avoid rank-changing slice/concat ops in `jax.random.gumbel` (`mode="highest"`).

In `float32` `mode="highest"`, `_gumbel` draws `(2, *shape)` random `uint32` bits and bounces between `(2, *shape)` and `*shape` via `neg[1]`, `jnp.array([...])` carry restacking, `jnp.where`, and `lax.clz(bits)` before unpacking `(hi, lo)` in `_safe_int_to_float`. Those rank-changing slice and concat ops prevent XLA from fusing Gumbel sampling into downstream reductions (such as `categorical`'s `argmax`), materializing `(2, *shape)` intermediates to HBM and recomputing the PRNG.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Reuse compiled shapes in Bessel `jn`/`yn` tests to avoid shard timeouts

`_jn` and `_yn` in `jax._src.scipy.bessel` are `@custom_jvp` functions wrapping `@partial(jit, static_argnums=(0,))`. Calling `jax.vmap(jax.grad(fn))` traces `_jn`/`_yn` on 0D scalars through `_pjit_batcher`, bypassing the 1D `@jit` cache already populated by forward/JVP calls and triggering redundant full XLA compilations of the Bessel recurrence graphs. Similarly, calling `_yn` or its JVP/grad on secondary test arrays (`imag_zs`, `overflow_zs`, and scalar `0.0`/`tiny_x`) with different lengths than the primary test array compiles additional executables per order.

Evaluate elementwise gradients on the 1D input array directly via `jax.grad(lambda x: jnp.sum(fn(x)))` and pad secondary test arrays to match the primary input shape so all checks reuse the cached 1D executables.

Add `jax.lax.exp2m1` and `jax.lax.log2p1` (and their core primitives) to compute `2**x - 1` and `log2(1 + x)` directly on real floating-point arrays, as specified by IEEE 754-2019.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] Fall back to `exp` in `erfc_default_impl` when native `exp2` lowering is unavailable

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Fall back to `exp` in `erfc_default_impl` when native `exp2` lowering is unavailable

When `ctx.is_forward_compat()`, `ifrt_version < 80`, or `libtpu < 0.0.52`, `lax.exp2(y)` lowers to `hlo.exponential(log(2) * y)` rather than `hlo.exp2`. Passing `use_exp2=True` to `erfc_default_impl` in that regime introduces an extra `float32` base-conversion rounding in `log(2) * y` on top of hardware `exp` range reduction.

Gate `use_exp2` in `_erfc_lowering` on native `hlo.exp2` availability so `erfc_default_impl` uses `exp(-s_hi)` (`use_exp2=False`) directly when `hlo.exp2` is unavailable, and update `ErfcTest.test_erfc_accurate_default_accuracy` with `float32` TPU bounds for `libtpu < 0.0.52`.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Upcast narrow signed integer indices before negative-index wrapping.

head_commit.message:
Upcast narrow signed integer indices before negative-index wrapping.

Indexing an axis whose length exceeds the maximum value of a narrow signed integer dtype (for example, indexing an axis longer than 127 elements with `jnp.int8(-1)`) previously wrapped the axis length and computed `index + size` within the narrow dtype, overflowing and selecting the wrong element (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42354).

To fix this, we promote narrow signed integer indices to an integer dtype wide enough to represent the target dimension before adding the axis length across dynamic slicing, `NDIndexer` gather/scatter normalization, `jnp.take`, and `jnp.put`. In addition, classify `jax.ds` slices with array or negative start offsets as dynamic slices in eager mode so negative start normalization behaves consistently with `jit`.

Fixes #42354 & #42377

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Restrict exported symbols in `libmosaic_gpu_runtime.so` via a linker version script to fix a segfault.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Restrict exported symbols in `libmosaic_gpu_runtime.so` via a linker version script to fix a segfault.

Since switching Linux wheel builds to statically linked `libc++` (`-lc++ -lc++abi -lunwind`), `libmosaic_gpu_runtime.so`—built with `-fvisibility=default` and no linker version script—has exported unversioned global `libc++abi` and `libc++` symbols (`__cxa_allocate_exception`, `__cxa_throw`, `__cxa_begin_catch`, `__cxa_end_catch`, `__gxx_personality_v0`). When a Mosaic GPU kernel is compiled in a wheel test worker, `custom_call.cc` loads `libmosaic_gpu_runtime.so` via `llvm::orc::DynamicLibrarySearchGenerator::Load` (`dlopen(..., RTLD_LAZY | RTLD_GLOBAL)`), interposing `libc++abi` symbols into the process-wide global symbol scope and causing a `SIGSEGV` when `libstdc++`-linked libraries such as `libcudnn` subsequently throw and catch C++ exceptions during `backend_compile_and_load`.

Add `mosaic_gpu_runtime.lds` so `libmosaic_gpu_runtime.so` exports only `mosaic_gpu_*` symbols and keeps all other symbols local.

Failed run: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/actions/runs/42615039323/job/129158448958|

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Support 128-lane A scale layout in tcgen05 on sm_107f.

head_commit.message:
Support 128-lane A scale layout in tcgen05 on sm_107f.

On `sm_107f`, `tcgen05.mma` supports a 128-lane Scale Factor A (`SFA`) layout in TMEM (enabled via bit 26 of the scaled instruction descriptor). The existing 32-lane layout has to be replicated across all four 32-lane TMEM partitions, so writing A scales from registers via `tcgen05.st` forces every warp to hold and store all 128 rows. With the 128-lane layout, row `r` lives in lane `r`, so each warp writes only its own rows, and the A scales take 4x fewer TMEM columns.

Add `scales_128_lane_layout()` in `tcgen05` (backed by `tmem_default_layout(packing=4)`), accept it for `a_scale` in `mma` on `sm_107f`, and set bit 26 in `_create_scaled_instr_descriptor` when it is used. Collective and sparse MMAs with this layout are rejected for now, since they are not covered by tests yet.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma on SM103.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support K=96 block-scaled FP4 tcgen05.mma on SM103.

On SM103 (`sm_103a`, GB300), dense 4-bit block-scaled `tcgen05.mma` (`mxf4` and `mxf4nvf4`) supports `K=96` (48 bytes per MMA step) in addition to `K=64` (32 bytes per MMA step), reducing the number of MMA instructions per K tile by up to 1.5× and lifting 2-CTA throughput from ~9.73 PFLOP/s to up to 14.62 PFLOP/s on 256×256×768 tiles.

`tcgen05.mma` now uses `K=96` steps on `sm_103a` for dense 4-bit block-scaled MMAs with SMEM operands and 128B swizzle, when `M=128`, the collective `N` is 128 or 256, and `b_scale` is not padded along `N`. All other configurations are unchanged.
